messages.subject: Rattle 2.6.21 released
messages.body_plain:
A new version Rattle has been released and is now available from CRAN.

To upgrade, start up R and:

> install.packages("rattle")

One of the major changes is that the Advanced Graphics option is now
on by default. Various plots are migrating to making use of the
ggplot2 package. Previous behaviour is restored by unselecting the
option in the Settings menu. Not all plots have been migrated yet.

Since the last announcement (2.6.17) there have also been many bug fixes.

A full change log is available as

  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/ChangeLog

A development version (updated more regularly) is available directly
from the Togaware repository:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

As always feedback, comments, suggestions are always welcome.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Error messages at Rattle startup
messages.body_plain:
Very odd - perhaps some interaction with a previously saved R session
- what happens when you start up R - do you see a message that it is
restoring a session?

You can check this on starting up R:

> ls()
character(0)

If you get a list of things then it is loading an old session

You could try renaming the .RData file (if any) in the default folder
and start up R and then Rattle again. The old session is stored there.

Or else, on starting up R:

> rm(list = ls())

to completely clean up the current session, then try starting up Rattle:

> library(rattle)

Regards,
Graham

After much rummaging I found that 3 environment variables - HOME, R_USER, R_LIBS_USER - were set to the problem directory, I don't know how or why.
By starting with a completely clean workspace and setting these variables to reasonable values, I now have rattle running with no problems.

messages.subject: A Question on Random Forests
messages.body_plain:
I really like Random Forests, but they are temperamental.   As a little background, I take several months of transaction history and use it to project a status the next month. For this one type of model I build, RF consistently gives great results.  The problem I have, that really limits its use in a production environment, is the factors.  If the new file doesn't have the exact same factors as the training file, the model errors out.  Even if the new model has a subset of factors, the model will fail.  Also, sometimes the new file, even if it has the same factors as the original training file, will give really strange answers that are only solved when I take the training file, delete all the rows and add in the rows from the new file.

Has anyone had similar issues?  Any suggestion on workarounds besides making sure the input file has the same factors are the training file?  Is there anything in Rattle that can be used to help here, like identifying when and where there's a factor issue?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: A Question on Random Forests
messages.body_plain:
You're just scoring new data?

Try stacking the new data with the original training data., scoring the combined dataset, and then tossing all the records from the original training set.

That will ensure that all the factors found in the training set will also be found in the scoring set. It will not of course ensure that the new data doesn't have any previously unseen factor values that were not found in the training dataset.

Depending on how much pre-processing you're doing, you might have to pre-process the new data, export it, combine it with the training data outside of Rattle, and bring the combined data back in.

HTH, I haven't had to do this myself.

d.d.
